guitar.evidence: Freddie King is well documented as primarily playing a Gibson ES-345 (and earlier Les Paul Goldtops) with a National fingerpick and thumbpick technique; a blues guitar icon.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown; well-established blues history fact.

tone.target: raw blues lead with gritty amp bite and vocal sustain
tone.profile: raw blues lead with gritty amp bite and vocal sustain
tone.summary: A vintage blues setup using a small combo amp model (UK 50/AC30 style) with light overdrive for grit, coupled with a wah pedal for expressive lead work and spring reverb for authentic sustain.

rig.name: Freddie King - I'm Tore Down - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide light grit and mid-range boost for blues bite.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD would also work, but Green OD offers a slightly more vintage/mid-focused tone suitable for Freddie King's style.

blocks.purpose: Add expressive vocal wah for lead lines.
blocks.gap: The C-Wah or B-Wah could also be used, but V-Wah is generally versatile and suitable for blues leads.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and focused on natural tube breakup/overdrive.
blocks.gap: No dedicated distortion needed; the Green OD handles the required grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a small, punchy tube combo amp (AC30 style) with classic blues character.
blocks.gap: The AC30 TB is the closest model, but UK 50 provides a slightly more compact and focused sound for this specific genre.

blocks.purpose: Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the UK 50 amp model.
blocks.gap: None. This pairing is standard for vintage blues tones.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the mid-range to enhance 'mid bite' and cut through the mix.
blocks.gap: None. Mid-scooping is often avoided in blues, so a slight lift is preferred.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle, authentic spring reverb for vocal sustain and depth.
blocks.gap: The Plate or Room reverb could work, but Spring is the most characteristic choice for vintage blues/rock.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better match the vintage blues tone.

proposals.reason: The UK Vintage 4x12 is too modern; a vintage speaker cabinet will enhance the raw blues bite.
